result.headline: No control fault shown; attitude loops track setpoints through aggressive manoeuvres, only start-up warnings recorded.
result.explanation: Roll, pitch and yaw follow their setpoints with a constant lag. The roll 'shift' at 16.3 s and the actuator steps are manoeuvre responses. Only start-up warnings and a constant airspeed of 0 are unexplained.

evidence.quote: SHIFT control.attitude_setpoint[roll] changed level for good at t=16.295 s: median 39.63 before, 2.555 after deg (7.1x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Roll setpoint moved, but the measured roll followed it (44.85 to -21.86 setpoint, 48.2 to -19.9 measured) and tracking error did not worsen (ratio 0.83).

evidence.quote: TRACKING control.attitude_setpoint[roll] vs vehicle.attitude[roll]: steady lag 0.949 s removed (a constant lag is this recording's normal, not a fault); typical |error| 2.295 deg, worst 21.022 at t=31.811 s; 6 window(s) above 6.884
evidence.shows: Roll tracks its setpoint (correlation 0.984 at the 0.949 s lag), so the roll loop is working.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[3]] at t=19.078 s: 1487 -> 1523 us (step 36, 9x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Channels 3, 4 and 5 stepped together during the roll manoeuvre. Attitude tracking error did not rise after 19.078 s (ratios 0.47 to 0.61).

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.578 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: The only warnings are at start-up (0.578 s, together with 'Sensor helth'). No later event follows them.

checked.check: compare at 16.295 s: what changed after the roll setpoint shift
checked.result: Roll measured followed the setpoint. Nothing froze. Tracking ratios were 1.04 (pitch), 0.83 (roll) and 0.22 (yaw).

checked.check: compare at 19.078 s: actuator step on channels 3, 4 and 5
checked.result: No output froze. Tracking improved (ratios 0.47 to 0.61). The step matches the roll manoeuvre.

checked.check: sequence 14 to 22 s: earliest signal to leave baseline
checked.result: Setpoints left baseline first at 14.089 s. Measured velocity, attitude, throttle and actuators followed, and roll attitude left last at 17.263 s. This is the order of a commanded manoeuvre.

checked.check: relation roll setpoint vs roll attitude over the recording
checked.result: Correlation 0.792 at zero lag and 0.984 at a 0.949 s lag, typical difference 6.08 deg.

effects.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch[1]] at t=26.914 s: 1482 -> 1548 us (step 66, 13.2x its usual variation)
effects.why: The roll-serving output moves with the roll setpoint (correlation -0.749), so this is a response.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[pitch] at t=30.036 s: 10.639 -> -14.386 deg (step -25.026, 6.7x its usual variation)
effects.why: The pitch setpoint stepped -27.1 deg at 28.699 s (line 46), so this is the lagged response.

outcomes.then: Close the control-fault question as no fault found

hypotheses.claim: Roll loop or its servo outputs failed around 16 to 19 s.
hypotheses.because: Roll follows its setpoint (correlation 0.984), no output froze, and tracking did not worsen after 16.295 s or 19.078 s.
hypotheses.observed_at: Controller attitude estimate and actuator command outputs

hypotheses.claim: A low-voltage condition affected the flight.
hypotheses.because: The warning appears only once at 0.578 s with no later effect visible. The data holds no voltage signal.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor was faulty: airspeed is constant at 0 and a 'Sensor helth' error fired at start-up.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed is constant at 0 and yaw rate is constant at 0 for the whole recording. This is not a change at an onset, and nothing downstream degraded.
Typical yaw error is 7 deg, with large excursions at start-up and at 8.9 s and 31.7 s. These were not individually tested.
